A household asks for a corridor first; only where access_corridor finds none may it be reached by passage

decisions.summary: While the share has room, standing houses offer tight seats at the footprints' parting plus 2 px, without the path's strip
decisions.why: The mechanism the MODE 1 ruling of 2026-10-03 required so that FR-002's 'MUST be able to seat' can happen; bounded by D4's share.

decisions.summary: A tight seat is taken only by passage; a household finding its own corridor there is refused it; ordinary seats keep a path's room
decisions.why: Excludes no household that could be reached across a yard; lane households keep the spacing the spec does not ask to change. D2-order applied at the tight seat.

decisions.summary: Tight seats offered only round a house a passage may cross to: reached within D3's chain and with a yard (passage.crossable)
decisions.why: A tight seat is taken only by passage (D2-tight-refusal), and a passage must end at a neighbor's yard whose house reaches the tree within PASSAGE_CHAIN (D2-walk, D3). A tight seat round any other house could seat no one, so the filter removes only seats that could never be taken; no household FR-002 allows is excluded.

decisions.summary: Tight seats offered only within TIGHT_BEARING_DEG 112.5 of the bearing from the house to its yard (front and flanks), not behind it
decisions.why: A narrowing: the research's condition (land with no road access) says nothing of which side of the neighbor's house it lies, so a household behind its neighbor's house can no longer be the one reached by passage. Legitimate on the spec's OWN rules, not on cost: FR-002 requires the walk never cross a house, bed, shed or fixture, and D2-walk keeps it on the two households' land, so from behind the house it must pass the house's flank clear of the beds and fixtures that stand there. Measured with every bearing offered (research R7, observed 2026-10-03): 1 walk to the yard found in 194 tries behind against 15 of 16 passages from within 90 degrees. The excluded sector is all but emptied by FR-002 itself; the restriction carries no historical claim (labeled a search breadth); a household behind its neighbor that finds a way of its own is not land the custom covers (D2-order); and 12 passage households on 8 of 13 settlements remain, so the purpose of US2 is not gutted. Cost is NOT the ground: the plan's 'offered there too the tight seats cost the homesteads stage 12-35%' is the whole every-bearing form against no passage (R7 row 1), and the yard-side form alone measured +18%, inside that range - the behind sector's own cost is not shown. That sentence must be restated as what R7 measured (the tries and the yield).

decisions.summary: Once one garden layout at a tight seat finds a corridor, the seat's other layouts are refused unasked
decisions.why: Narrower than a per-layout verdict: a layout whose beds block its own way, with a walk, is refused because another layout at the seat has a way. Legitimate on the same ground as D2-order: Wigmore's condition is the LAND's - land that cannot reach the highway without passing over another's - and the plan's land is the seat's reach over every garden layout (D2-adjoin). A seat from which a way of its own exists is land with road access; a garden arrangement that blocks one's own path does not make the land landlocked. Note: the plan's and fit.py's '93 of 106 corridor searches after a walk' appears nowhere in research R7 (R7: 55 asked, 43 found; R6: 90 asked, 75 found); record it or correct it.

decisions.summary: The reach is the custom's condition: the household's land (the reach its seat was parted by, over every layout) within the parting and PASSAGE_ADJOIN_FT of the neighbor's footprint, a GUESS
decisions.why: Unchanged: land against land, the spec's 'across a neighbor's dooryard' read literally; makes FR-002 reachable rather than restricting it (R6).

decisions.summary: The walk from a dooryard door to the neighbor's threshing yard, on the two households' land, clear of houses, beds, sheds, byres, well pockets, fixtures, other homesteads, refused ground and wood seats, routed; not drawn as a lane (GUESS)
decisions.why: Unchanged: FR-002's clearances and US2's 'no lane of its own'; routing removes a restriction the request never asked for (R6).
